name: Terminal-Bench 1.0
description: Complete multi-step tasks in a terminal; task-specific tests inspect the final environment.
input: Terminal task instruction and a prepared container
output: Shell actions and resulting files or system state
date_note: The May announcement calls the original suite Core-v0; the 2.0 announcement calls the May release 1.0. These are not separate launch dates.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
description: Complete harder terminal tasks with independently checked final outcomes. The 2.0 release introduced a new task suite and Harbor.
input: A task brief and a configured terminal environment
output: Files, program outputs or a changed environment
assessment: Share of tasks completed under their task-specific verifiers.
date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
description: Run the revised 2.0 suite. The authors corrected 28 of its 89 tasks, so matching the model alone does not make scores comparable.
input: An 89-task terminal suite with corrected task definitions
assessment: Task completion under the corrected instructions and verifiers.
date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

name: Terminal-Bench 3.0
description: Complete 74 challenging terminal workflows drawn from seven domains in the first 3.0 task set.
input: A work request and a configured terminal environment
output: A verified artifact or state change
assessment: Pass rate under the 3.0 task verifiers.
date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: GitHub release published_at (UTC); the project announcement has its own later date.

name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
description: The 4.0 release removes eight 3.0 tasks, fixes others and recalibrates compute and time limits.
input: The 66-task terminal suite and its 4.0 resource settings
assessment: Share of tasks passing the 4.0 checks under the specified resources.
date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: GitHub release published_at (UTC); the project announcement has its own later date.

name: Terminal-Bench 4.1
description: The agent-facing 4.0 tasks remain the same; revised verifiers regrade the resulting artifacts.
input: The same 66 agent-facing terminal tasks as 4.0
assessment: Share passing the revised 4.1 verifiers; saved 4.0 outputs can be regraded.
date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: GitHub release published_at (UTC); the project announcement has its own later date.

name: τ-bench
description: Converse with a simulated customer and call tools; check the final database state against the goal.
input: Simulated customer, domain policy, tools and database
output: Tool actions and messages to the customer
assessment: Final database state and required reply contents checked

name: τ²-bench
description: Coordinate with a simulated user who can also change the environment. The original τ² release adds a dual-control telecom domain.
input: A support request, domain policies, tools and a simulated user
output: A conversation and tool actions that complete the task
assessment: End-state checks and required outputs; pass^k measures consistent success across repeated attempts.
date_note: Sierra announcement. This is not the October 2026 release called τ-bench 2.0.0.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: arXiv v1 submission before the June 10 announcement.

name: τ²-bench 0.1.3
description: A τ² revision that removes default natural-language assertion checks. Specify the grading version when comparing results that depend on those checks.
input: A policy, support request and interactive tool environment
assessment: State and tool checks under the 0.1.3 defaults; natural-language assertions no longer run by default.
date_note: GitHub published release; the changelog documents the grading default.

name: τ³-bench
description: Extend agent–user tasks to support-document retrieval and real-time spoken interaction. This public suite corresponds to repository release v1.0.0.
input: A text or spoken support request, domain tools and policies or a knowledge base
output: A response and effective changes in the customer-support environment
assessment: Task-specific completion checks and repeated-run reliability, reported by domain and interface.
date_note: Sierra announcement and matching GitHub release; not the original 2024 τ-bench.

name: τ-bench 1.0.1
description: A grading revision to the τ³ generation. It corrects banking knowledge task data and evaluation; the authors say the other domains are unaffected.
input: A support interaction with domain tools; banking tasks also have a policy corpus
assessment: Revised banking task and rubric checks. Pre-1.0.1 banking scores are not directly comparable.
date_note: Public GitHub release dated July 22 UTC. Some fixes reached main on July 14–15 without a version bump; this row dates the named release, not an individual fix.

name: τ-bench 2.0.0
description: Evaluate text and voice interactions across languages using pinned task manifests. The official release changes task prompts, judging and caller configuration.
input: A text or voice support request, domain tools and a language-specific environment
output: A dialogue and task-specific environment updates
assessment: Completion and consistency on the named text or voice manifest; 1.x scores are not interchangeable.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: GitHub published_at is Oct 20 00:28 UTC. The release body and dated changelog state October 19.

name: ARC-AGI-1
description: Infer a new transformation rule from example grids; reproduce the target grid without a written instruction.
input: Example input/output grid pairs and a test grid
assessment: Grid dimensions and all cell values must match
date_note: Original paper v1; ARC-AGI-1 is the later official name for this edition.

name: ARC-AGI-2
description: Infer a transformation rule from example grid pairs and apply it to a new grid.
input: Example input/output grid pairs and a test input
assessment: Dimensions and every cell must match the target

name: ARC-AGI-3 Preview
description: Explore an early set of interactive games and infer their rules. This developer preview and its competition are distinct from the full 2026 benchmark.
input: Grid observations from the preview games
output: A sequence of legal game actions
assessment: The preview competition ranked performance on held-back games by levels completed, with tie-breaks; not the full 2026 RHAE score.
date_note: Retrospective from the maintainer explicitly dates the public preview to July 17. The competition kickoff was July 18.

name: ARC-AGI-3
description: Explore an unfamiliar game, infer its goals and advance through levels. A solver can write code, but the benchmark grades its actions, not its source code.
input: Observations from an unfamiliar interactive environment
output: Actions that reach the level goals
assessment: Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), using human action baselines
date_note: Official full benchmark launch on March 25. The technical report was submitted March 24; the preview was released July 17, 2025.

alternative_dated_evidence.note: arXiv v1 submission, not the full launch event.

name: APEX-Agents 1.0
description: Produce a professional deliverable in a shared workspace for a banking, consulting or legal assignment. This is the agent benchmark, not the tool-free APEX suite.
input: A professional brief, files and workplace applications
output: A client-ready answer or work product
assessment: Expert rubrics: full-task pass rate and mean criterion score
date_note: Original launch of APEX-Agents; distinct from the APEX umbrella and tool-free APEX-1.

name: APEX-Agents 1.1
description: Deliver professional work from a document-rich environment. Version 1.1 refines the tasks and judges ambiguous or contradictory answers differently.
input: A work brief, reference files and workplace tools
assessment: Expert-authored rubric criteria; report mean rubric score or full-task pass rate with the 1.1 grading protocol.
